A complete cycle

Help › Examples › Rankine cycle is a whole problem on one sheet. Water is the working fluid, the pump is isentropic, and the turbine has an isentropic efficiency of 0.86. This page shows the whole sheet, then follows it in the order of a solution on paper.

The whole sheet

%% Rankine cycle with turbine efficiency
% Water is the working fluid. The turbine has an isentropic efficiency;
% the pump is isentropic.
fluid water

%% Given values
p_b   = 70 [bar]       % boiler pressure
T_1   = 520 [C]        % turbine inlet temperature
p_c   = 0.1 [bar]      % condenser pressure
eta_t = 0.86           % turbine isentropic efficiency

%% States
% No pressure drop in the boiler and condenser: states 4 and 1 are at
% p_b, states 2 and 3 at p_c.
state 1  : p = p_b, T = T_1
% State 2s: the turbine exit if the expansion were isentropic.
state 2s : p = p_c, s = s_1
% The actual exit enthalpy follows from the turbine efficiency.
eta_t = (h_1 - h_2) / (h_1 - h_2s)
state 2  : p = p_c, h = h_2
% State 3: saturated liquid leaves the condenser.
state 3  : p = p_c, x = 0
% State 4: the pump is isentropic, so s_4 = s_3.
state 4  : p = p_b, s = s_3

%% Work and heat transfer per unit mass of steam
% Each component: steady state, kinetic and potential energy changes
% neglected. Each amount is positive, with its direction in its name.
% Turbine, no stray heat transfer. w_t: turbine work per unit mass
% flowing, Ẇ_t/ṁ.
w_t   = h_1 - h_2      % turbine
% Pump, no stray heat transfer. w_p: pump work per unit mass, Ẇ_p/ṁ.
w_p   = h_4 - h_3      % pump
% Boiler, no work. q_in: heat transfer to the steam per unit mass, Q̇_in/ṁ.
q_in  = h_1 - h_4      % boiler
% Condenser, no work. q_out: heat transfer from the steam per unit
% mass, Q̇_out/ṁ.
q_out = h_2 - h_3      % condenser
% w_net: net work per unit mass, Ẇ_cycle/ṁ.
w_net = w_t - w_p

%% Performance
eta = w_net / q_in     % thermal efficiency
bwr = w_p / w_t        % back work ratio

%% Energy balance of the cycle
check q_in - q_out == w_net

%% T-s diagram
% A -s- path between states whose entropies differ is drawn dashed, as for
% the actual expansion 1-2.
plot Ts : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3 -s- 4 -p- 1
% Change T_1 to 560 C and watch eta and x_2.

Copy the sheet into Dome, or open it from the Help menu. Dome gives w_net = 1099.3 kJ/kg, eta = 0.33711 and bwr = 0.0063737, and the check line shows "passed".

  1. A line that starts with %% names a part of the solution: the given values, the states, the work and heat transfer, and so on.
  2. A line that starts with % is a comment. The comments state the assumptions, as a solution on paper does.
  3. Each section below shows the lines it explains, what Dome gives for them, and the rules they follow.

Given values

%% Given values
p_b   = 70 [bar]       % boiler pressure
T_1   = 520 [C]        % turbine inlet temperature
p_c   = 0.1 [bar]      % condenser pressure
eta_t = 0.86           % turbine isentropic efficiency

A given value shows nothing at the right of its line, since the line states it. The Workspace lists each one with its unit.

  1. A line name = number [unit] is an input of the sheet. A number written in a state line is one too: the x = 0 of state 3 makes x_3 an input.
  2. An efficiency is a plain number with no unit. Write 0.86, not 86; When Dome refuses shows what 86 gives.
  3. An input can be swept over a range of values (see Sweeps). Some inputs can also be dragged on a diagram, as the T–s diagram shows.

States

%% States
% No pressure drop in the boiler and condenser: states 4 and 1 are at
% p_b, states 2 and 3 at p_c.
state 1  : p = p_b, T = T_1
% State 2s: the turbine exit if the expansion were isentropic.
state 2s : p = p_c, s = s_1
% The actual exit enthalpy follows from the turbine efficiency.
eta_t = (h_1 - h_2) / (h_1 - h_2s)
state 2  : p = p_c, h = h_2
% State 3: saturated liquid leaves the condenser.
state 3  : p = p_c, x = 0
% State 4: the pump is isentropic, so s_4 = s_3.
state 4  : p = p_b, s = s_3

Dome gives the phase or the quality at the right of each state line. State 2s has x = 0.828 and state 2 has x = 0.904; state 4 is a compressed liquid. The efficiency line gives h_2 = 2353.5 kJ/kg.

  1. The line fluid water, near the top of the sheet, sets the fluid of the state lines after it.
  2. A state line fixes a state from two properties and defines p_1, T_1, v_1, u_1, h_1, s_1 and x_1. State lines gives the pairs that fix a state.
  3. A property may be given by a name: s = s_1 gives state 2s the entropy of state 1, as an isentropic expansion has.
  4. A label is made of letters, digits and underscores, such as 2s. The properties of state 2s are p_2s, h_2s, s_2s and so on.
  5. The efficiency line has one unknown, h_2. Dome solves it, and h_2 then fixes state 2 with p_c. The lines may come in any order.
  6. The states table under the sheet gives every property of every state.

Work and heat transfer

%% Work and heat transfer per unit mass of steam
% Each component: steady state, kinetic and potential energy changes
% neglected. Each amount is positive, with its direction in its name.
% Turbine, no stray heat transfer. w_t: turbine work per unit mass
% flowing, Ẇ_t/ṁ.
w_t   = h_1 - h_2      % turbine
% Pump, no stray heat transfer. w_p: pump work per unit mass, Ẇ_p/ṁ.
w_p   = h_4 - h_3      % pump
% Boiler, no work. q_in: heat transfer to the steam per unit mass, Q̇_in/ṁ.
q_in  = h_1 - h_4      % boiler
% Condenser, no work. q_out: heat transfer from the steam per unit
% mass, Q̇_out/ṁ.
q_out = h_2 - h_3      % condenser
% w_net: net work per unit mass, Ẇ_cycle/ṁ.
w_net = w_t - w_p

%% Performance
eta = w_net / q_in     % thermal efficiency
bwr = w_p / w_t        % back work ratio

Dome gives w_t = 1106.3 kJ/kg, w_p = 7.0513 kJ/kg, q_in = 3260.9 kJ/kg and q_out = 2161.6 kJ/kg. Then w_net = 1099.3 kJ/kg, eta = 0.33711 and bwr = 0.0063737.

  1. Each component's energy balance is one line. The comment above it names the assumptions that reduce the balance to that line.
  2. Each amount is positive, with its direction in its name: q_in is the heat transfer to the steam, and q_out the heat transfer from it.
  3. Each amount is per unit mass of steam: w_t is Ẇ_t/ṁ. For a rate, give the mass flow rate. With m_dot = 30 [kg/s], the line W_cycle = m_dot*w_net gives 32978 kW.
  4. The Workspace lists every result with its unit.

The energy balance check

%% Energy balance of the cycle
check q_in - q_out == w_net

For a cycle, the net heat transfer equals the net work. Dome shows "passed" at the right of the line, and the Checks tab lists the check as Passed.

  1. Dome evaluates a check line after the sheet is solved. This one confirms that the work and heat transfer lines agree with each other.
  2. A slip of sign or label makes it fail. With the q_out line written q_out = h_3 - h_2, the check shows "failed", and the Checks tab gives 5422.5 kJ/kg ≠ 1099.3 kJ/kg.
  3. Some slips leave the balance true. The efficiency line written upside down, eta_t = (h_1 - h_2s) / (h_1 - h_2), still passes the check.
  4. A check on the turbine catches that slip. An actual expansion ends at a higher enthalpy than the isentropic one, so write check h_2 > h_2s. With the slip, it fails: 1964 kJ/kg not > 2173.4 kJ/kg.

The T–s diagram

%% T-s diagram
% A -s- path between states whose entropies differ is drawn dashed, as for
% the actual expansion 1-2.
plot Ts : 1 -s- 2 -p- 3 -s- 4 -p- 1

Dome draws the cycle in the figure pane beside the sheet. The plot line shows the name of its figure at its right.

  1. Write plot Ts : and the states in the order of the cycle, joined by paths. The path -s- draws a process at constant s, and -p- one at constant p.
  2. -T-, -v- and -h- draw a process at constant T, v or h, and -- a straight line.
  3. A path whose property differs at its two ends is drawn dashed. Here s_2 differs from s_1, so the expansion 1–2 is dashed: only its end states are known.
  4. A path to a state the sheet does not have is not drawn. With 5 in place of 4, the figure pane shows "no state 5 in the sheet".
  5. State 1 is fixed by the input T_1, which the T axis shows, so state 1 can be dragged up and down. At the end of the drag, Dome writes the new value into the line T_1 = 520 [C].
  6. The other diagrams are Tv, pv, ph and hs. Diagrams gives the rules for all of them.

Changing an input

T_1   = 560 [C]        % turbine inlet temperature

The comment at the end of the sheet suggests this edit of the T_1 line. Dome then gives eta = 0.3424 and x_2 = 0.923, up from 0.33711 and 0.904.

  1. The edited line is tinted and shows the number it held before: was 520.
  2. Each result that changed shows the change beside its value. The line of eta shows 0.3424 +0.0053.
  3. The T–s diagram draws the previous run dashed, with a legend that names the change. The Previous run box of the figure pane turns this off.
  4. To follow a result over a whole range of T_1, run a sweep. Sweeps starts from this sheet.

When Dome refuses

Each entry changes or deletes one line of the Rankine example. It shows the line as changed, the message Dome shows, and what to change.

A sheet with no fluid line

state 1  : p = p_b, T = T_1

state 1 has no fluid: add a line "fluid water" (or another fluid) above it, or write "state 1 (water) : …"

The line fluid water was deleted. Every state line gets this message with its own label. The state 1 and state 3 lines also get a message that lists the fluids. Write fluid water above the first state line.

An efficiency written as a percentage

eta_t = 86           % turbine isentropic efficiency

state 2: water: no state has these values of p and h within the property data (0.01 °C to 1926.85 °C, up to 10000 bar)

The message is on the line state 2 : p = p_c, h = h_2. With eta_t = 86, the efficiency line gives an h_2 far below that of any water at 0.1 bar. Write eta_t = 0.86.

State 2 fixed as if the expansion were isentropic

state 2  : p = p_c, s = s_1

this equation contradicts the others (its two sides differ by 5.34 %)

The message is on the efficiency line, eta_t = (h_1 - h_2) / (h_1 - h_2s). With s = s_1, state 2 is state 2s, and the efficiency cannot be 0.86. Fix state 2 by h = h_2, the enthalpy the efficiency line finds.

A state line that repeats a given value

state 1  : p = p_b, T = 520 [C]

T_1 is already given on line 8

A number in a state line is an input, so T_1 is given twice: here and in the line T_1 = 520 [C]. Dome also warns that the state 1 line repeats the others. Write the name instead: T = T_1.

One label for two states

state 2  : p = p_c, x = 0

state 2 is defined twice

The state 3 line was changed to give state 2 a second time, so no line fixes state 3. Dome also reports that nothing determines s_3 and h_3. Give each state a label of its own.
